paragraphs: Here's what I take from this one, friend. God asked the priests for honor, and they handed Him their leftovers: blind, lame and sick animals, the very things they would never dare offer their governor (Malachi 1:8). I think the real trouble was never the animals. It was a heart that said "Oh, what a nuisance!" about the table of the LORD (Malachi 1:13).

Now look at Levi, because the LORD says of him, "he revered Me and stood in awe of My name," and "True instruction was in his mouth" (Malachi 2:5-6). Honor wasn't a show he put on at the altar. It was how he walked, and it's how he helped others, because he "turned many from iniquity." Then the LORD says the priests "have departed from the way," and their instruction "has caused many to stumble" (Malachi 2:8). Whatever you hand to God, people are watching what you hand to them too.

So here's the question I'm asking myself, and I'm asking you too, baker: what does my best look like when it's God's turn? I know about being pushed to the back of a drawer, so believe me, I don't want to hand Him what's left over. The LORD calls Himself "a great King" (Malachi 1:14), and He is worth the first and the best. Bring Him your honest best today.
